title: Knowledge sources
description: A venture's source map (<venture>/knowledge/sources.json, EE-037): the sources its records live in and which record types live where. Optional: a record type it does not name, and every record of a venture without one, lives in the venture's own folder (the implicit `venture` source). The venture decides its own layout; Mentura does not. Rules make it a source-of-truth matrix: a system of record per record type, attribute and context, written for a fast model to read (EE-042). Each source names a connector from the registry (an integration with a `connector` in packages/naive/src/records/layers/knowledge/tooling/integrations.json). Credentials are named by environment variable, never stored. Beside the sources Naive reads records from, `functions` says where each of the venture's functions keeps its truth outside Naive (EE-083): the repo, hosting and analytics for the product, a payments or store account for sales, the bank for money, a folder or signing service for legal documents. Those are pointers to systems of record; a system Naive reads through code is connected, one it only knows of is pointed. `truth` says where the venture's source of truth as a whole lives.

id.description: The source's id; `venture` is reserved for the venture's own folder

connector.description: An integration id with a connector: filesystem, github

carries.description: records (the default): the venture's records live there. signals: a signal library in the naive-signal-library@1 layout, read in place, whose signals reach records only through listeners (signal library design). Reading a paid library tells its publisher which signal types the venture hears

writes.description: How writes reach it; the connector's default when left out

root.description: filesystem: the folder, relative to the venture folder or absolute. github: the folder inside the repository

token.description: github: the environment variable holding a token (default GITHUB_TOKEN)

api.description: github: the API base, for GitHub Enterprise

search.description: github: code search (default) or a scan of the files

records.description: Record type id (from packages/naive/src/records/data-model.json) -> source id. Unnamed record types stay in the venture folder.

rules.description: The source-of-truth matrix (EE-042). Each rule is one cell: for one record type in one context, its system of record and owner. Every field is present and "*" means any, so a fast model reads a rule without inferring anything. The rule with the most fields that are not "*" wins; two that tie fail the check. `records` is shorthand for rules that match anything.

record.description: A venture record type id from packages/naive/src/records/data-model.json

attribute.description: "*" for the whole record, or one top-level field mastered elsewhere (such as price). The router reads the field from that source and writes it there, kept at the record's own path as a JSON object holding only that field; the record's own file does not keep a copy.

phase.description: The venture's phase this rule holds in

system_of_record.description: A source id from `sources`, or venture for the venture's own folder

owner.description: The role accountable for this cell's data (the MDM data owner), a role id from governance decision rights or the team plan

survivorship.description: When the same record also lives in other sources, which value wins. Running these rules across vendors is the platform's; the framework only states and checks them.

truth.description: local: this device is the source of truth; otherwise the address of the host every system is backed up to or hosted on (EE-083)

functions.description: Each function's systems of record, by department id (packages/naive/src/functions/departments.json) or legal (EE-083)

source.description: The source in `sources` that reads it, when it is one

status.description: connected: read by code (a connector or an integration); pointed: known, not read yet

fixture.description: The last sync replayed a saved answer, not the live system

note.description: What the founder said about this function, in their words
